routes.description: Establish reasonable theism through a cumulative inference that a personal transcendent source better explains cosmic origins and fine-tuning, consciousness and rationality, objective morality and dignity, and the intelligibility of evil than naturalism does.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its principal phenomena remain evidentially significant, the theistic account explains them with greater unity and adequacy than the relevant naturalistic alternatives, and objections concerning suffering and religious history do not defeat the resulting reasonableness claim.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative comparative case to reasonable belief in general theism without requiring that any single argument prove Christianity or establish certainty.

centralBridges.description: Show that cosmic beginning conditions and life-permitting fine-tuning are better explained by a transcendent intelligent cause than by physical self-sufficiency, chance, or brute fact.
Show that consciousness and truth-directed rational faculties fit a reality grounded in supreme mind better than strict materialist naturalism.
Show that objective value, duty, and intrinsic human dignity require a foundation supplied by God's non-arbitrary good character and the divine image.

Explain why suffering and religious corruption do not overturn the cumulative case, including how objective evil remains intelligible and how abuses may be distinguished from Christianity's proper ethical standard.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend the relevance of comparing theism with representative naturalistic commitments while acknowledging that cosmological evidence initially supports general rather than specifically biblical theism.
Support the moral case by clarifying disputed Christian teachings and identifying internal resources for moral correction and reform.

routes.description: Deny that the cumulative case makes belief in God reasonable by showing that its empirical and philosophical inferences are underdetermined, that naturalistic alternatives remain available, and that suffering and the historical record of religious explanation count against the proposed God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative phenomena do not discriminate adequately in favor of a personal benevolent creator, unresolved questions cannot properly be converted into theistic evidence, and the counterevidence from natural history and religious performance substantially weakens the cumulative inference.

motionBridge.description: Show that gaps in present naturalistic explanation and the bare compatibility of phenomena with theism do not satisfy the burden for reasonable belief in God.

centralBridges.description: Challenge both an absolute cosmic beginning and the probabilistic design inference by presenting the universe's scale, repeated opportunities, and divine omnipotence as complications for fine-tuning evidence.
Show that naturalism and atheism need not entail a single strict materialist package, so uncertainty about consciousness, freedom, or abstract objects is not affirmative evidence for God.
Argue that cosmic vastness, evolutionary waste, extinction, and pervasive suffering are less expected under an omnipotent benevolent creator than under naturalism.
Argue that the replacement of religious explanations and the revision of inherited moral teachings undermine claims of reliable revelation and superior theistic explanation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Offer evolutionary accounts of moral sentiments and invoke the Euthyphro challenge to contest the claim that objective morality uniquely requires God.
Explain religious moral change as externally pressured adaptation or selective survival rather than evidence that fixed religious authority reliably generates reform.

sections.title: Cumulative Inference and the Scope of the Worldview Comparison
sections.rationale: Frames what must be shown for belief to be reasonable, whether an inference to the best explanation may aggregate several clues, and which forms of theism and naturalism are legitimately compared.

sections.title: Cosmic Origins, Scale, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: Tests whether beginning conditions and life-permitting parameters favor a transcendent designer or remain underdetermined given cosmic scale, chance opportunities, uncertainty about an absolute beginning, and divine omnipotence.

sections.title: Consciousness, Rational Faculties, and Naturalistic Commitments
sections.rationale: Examines whether consciousness and truth-directed reasoning require a supreme mind, whether evolution undermines cognitive reliability, and whether naturalism must accept the strict materialism targeted by those arguments.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Character, and Human Dignity
sections.rationale: Addresses whether objective value, obligation, and intrinsic human worth need a divine foundation, alongside the Euthyphro dilemma and evolutionary or goal-relative naturalistic accounts of morality.

sections.title: Evil, Suffering, and the Shape of Natural History
sections.rationale: Weighs evolutionary suffering, extinction, cosmic vastness, and apparent waste against the claim that evil presupposes objective norms and can ultimately be defeated within a theistic framework.

sections.title: Religious Explanation, Revelation, and Moral Reform
sections.rationale: Evaluates Christianity's asserted moral influence and internal corrective resources against alleged explanatory displacement, disputed teachings, institutional resistance to reform, and revision of positions concerning women and sexuality.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: The universe's finite beginning and lack of physical self-sufficiency point to a transcendent cause beyond the physical universe.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Life-permitting, life-producing, and life-sustaining fine-tuning is more expected if an intelligent and powerful creator guides the universe than if it occurs without guidance.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Conscious experience is difficult to derive from matter alone but fits naturally within a worldview grounded in a supreme mind.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Naturalistic evolution oriented toward survival does not secure truth-directed rational faculties, whereas creation in the image of a rational God can ground generally reliable reasoning.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: If strict naturalism explains moral beliefs only as evolved feelings, it cannot thereby ground objective duties, value, agency, or human dignity.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Evil presupposes objective norms unavailable to strict naturalism, while relationship with infinite divine goodness supplies a good capable of ultimately defeating suffering and horror.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Taken together, cosmic origins and fine-tuning, consciousness, rationality, objective morality, and Christianity's moral influence make theism a better overall explanation than naturalism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Strict materialism is the mainstream form of naturalism, while broader naturalisms that affirm consciousness, freedom, and objective value draw on resources more at home in theism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: The Euthyphro challenge presents a false dilemma because goodness is grounded non-arbitrarily in God's character and moral duties arise from commands expressing that character.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Biblical texts do not impose a general ban on women's public ministry, because restrictive readings depend on disputed translation, interpolation, or neglect of textual and historical context.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Religious corruption should be judged against Jesus, whose authority, ethic, and solidarity with marginalized people provide Christianity's proper corrective standard.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Cosmic vastness, evolutionary waste, extinction, and pervasive suffering are improbable products of an omnipotent and benevolent creator.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: The repeated replacement of religious explanations by successful natural explanations gives theism a poor explanatory track record.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Scriptural and traditional subordination of women undermines claims of objective, timeless morality and reliable divine communication.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: The universe's immense scale and repeated opportunities for unlikely outcomes favor atheism rather than providing discriminating evidence for divine design.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Naturalism does not entail materialism or a settled account of consciousness, so uncertainty about consciousness cannot fairly be treated as evidence for God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Naturalists and atheists hold diverse positions on materialism, free will, and abstract objects, so a uniform materialist characterization does not represent the skeptical worldview.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Christian moral dominance preserved serious injustices until Enlightenment opposition, while the Euthyphro dilemma prevents God from uniquely grounding morality.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: The Big Bang is not established as the beginning of everything, and divine omnipotence undercuts the inference from fine-tuning to God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Evolution explains cooperative moral feelings and their changing social boundaries better than a fixed theistic moral framework does.
